newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: ARGENTINE STOCKS END WITH MODEST RISE, SEEN FIRM.
newsitem.headline: ARGENTINE STOCKS END WITH MODEST RISE, SEEN FIRM.

text.p: Argentine stocks recouped early losses to close slightly higher Monday and traders expected prices to remain steady.
"The market is weathering volatility on the international markets and will continue to aim higher," said Jose Napoli at brokers Ignoto y Napoli.
The blue-chip MerVal index pulled off a low of 842 to close at 853.29 with a gain of 0.3 percent.
Napoli said he expected the index would soon pierce its five-year high of 857 set last Wednesday.
But traders said the session's slim volume denoted underlying caution ahead of the release of U.S. retail sales and inflation data Wednesday and Thursday.

"I think the U.S. indicators will be more or less in line with expectations, and as soon as the New York markets find their feet the bolsa should test new highs," said Jorge Bonanno at brokers Interfin.
Floor volume shrank to 17.5 million pesos from already weak tally of 22 million Friday, while over-the-counter turnover totaled 111.5 million pesos compared to 97.2 million Friday.
The broad market firmed 0.2 percent, but losers still edged out winners 22 to 20 and 21 stocks closed flat.
Main-tier gains were led by foods giant Molinos Rio de la Plata, Banco de Galicia and steelmaker Siderca, which jumped 3.7 percent, 2.9 percent and 2.4 percent, respectively.
The heaviest MerVal loser was carmaker Sevel, which tumbled 4.7 percent after the company reported a first-half net loss of $44.8 million.
Bansud bank fell 3.1 percent and textile and footwear firm Alpargatas shed 1.7 percent.
